gaps: Platform panel: Apply was never reached, because the second checkbox toggle destroys the panel first. What a committed multi-platform selection does to the chip label, the count line and the 26-row list is therefore unverified.
Baseline date chip: no option was ever picked in the state map, so its Apply/commit behaviour — and whether the chip correctly drops the '(default)' suffix — is unknown.
Close-without-Apply was never exercised on a freshly added chip: whether a Platform chip that was added but never applied stays parked on the bar with no value is unrecorded.

The status segmented control and the dashboard deep-link chip sit directly above this bar but are outside my slice. Segments commit on click while every bar chip is Apply-gated; that mixed commit model on one screen could not be assessed from the map I was given.
No loading or error state exists in this local demo, so nothing can be said about what the bar shows when a filter query is slow or fails.

findings.element: Platform multiselect panel in #recFilterBar — second checkbox toggle (e.g. Shopify after Stripe)
findings.finding: Ticking a second checkbox in the Platform panel closes the panel and silently discards the whole selection, so Apply can never be reached with more than one platform chosen.
findings.user_impact: The stated task — narrowing the list to the platforms you care about — cannot be completed: the user ticks a second platform, the panel vanishes with no message, the list still shows all 26 rows, and reopening the chip shows nothing selected.
findings.suggested_fix: In the checkbox change handler, update the checked box in place instead of calling refreshFieldNode with keepOpen — the keepOpen path runs closeLayerTree first, which fires the previously registered close handler (onPanelClose → draft reset → a second re-render), leaving the panel that gets re-marked 'active' detached from the DOM.

evidence.action: Added the Platform filter via 'Add filter', then clicked 'Stripe' (step 1) and 'Shopify' (step 2) in the panel, asserting panel visibility and Apply hittability in real Chromium; then traced the handler at wireFieldNode → refreshFieldNode({keepOpen:true}) in the source.
evidence.observed: After step 1 the panel stayed visible and Apply was hittable. After step 2 the panel was no longer visible and Apply was not hittable; the Shopify selection was never committed, and no error, toast or chip state indicated anything had happened.

findings.finding: A chip loses its dropdown caret the moment it holds a value, so an applied filter looks like a read-only summary tag rather than a control you can reopen and edit.
findings.user_impact: A user who wants to change Stripe to PayPal sees no affordance for editing and is pushed to remove the chip with '×' and rebuild it through 'Add filter' — three extra steps for what is one click on the chip.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the dropdown caret on the chip trigger when the chip is active, alongside the '×', so the chip reads as editable-plus-removable in both states.

evidence.action: Inspected the chip render branch of fieldHtml (style 'chip') for an active vs inactive value, and the chip-trigger click handler in wireFieldNode.
evidence.observed: The caret span is emitted only when the field is inactive — `(active ? '' : 'arrow_drop_down')` — while the chip-trigger button still opens the panel in both states. The only visible glyph on an applied chip is the '×' remove button.

findings.element: Baseline date chip 'Last 90 days (default)' → date panel (6 relative presets + Apply)
findings.finding: The date panel offers only relative presets — All time, Last 7/30/90 days, This month, Last month — with no custom or absolute range, so no specific historical period can be selected.
findings.user_impact: An accountant reconciling a past quarter or a prior tax year has no way to ask for it; the only reach beyond last month is 'All time', which drops them into an unbounded list they must scan manually.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Custom range' option to the date panel with direct month and year selection, so a historical window is reachable without month-by-month stepping and without falling back to 'All time'.

evidence.action: Opened the baseline date chip per the state map and enumerated its options against the FILTERS.date definition in the source, checking against KF-3 (date pickers covering historical ranges need direct month/year selection).
evidence.observed: Exactly six relative options are rendered, all anchored to today; there is no custom-range entry, no month or year selector, and the oldest bounded window available is 'Last month'.
